column6: Je mets de l'ail dans la sauce.
column7: I put garlic in the sauce.
column8: Masculine; as an ingredient it takes the partitive: de l'ail.

column6: Elle coupe une courgette en rondelles.
column7: She cuts a courgette into slices.
column8: A feminine noun; the British English word is borrowed from French.

column6: Ce soir, nous mangeons une aubergine grillée.
column7: Tonight we are eating a grilled aubergine.
column8: Feminine; British English also says aubergine, American English says eggplant.

column6: Il reste une seule nouille dans l'assiette.
column7: There is only one noodle left on the plate.
column8: Feminine; usually used in the plural: des nouilles.

column6: Elle ajoute de la crème dans la soupe.
column7: She adds cream to the soup.
column8: Feminine; it also covers custards and cosmetic creams.

column6: Je mets du miel dans mon yaourt.
column7: I put honey in my yoghurt.
column8: Masculine; the final l is pronounced.

column6: Nous mangeons du thon avec du riz.
column7: We are eating tuna with rice.
column8: Masculine; it is spelled with th but pronounced as a plain t.

column6: Nous mangeons du saumon ce soir.
column7: We are eating salmon tonight.
column8: Masculine; as a colour word it is invariable.

column6: J'ai mis une noix dans mon sac.
column7: I put a walnut in my bag.
column8: Feminine; the plural is identical: des noix. It also appears in noix de coco.

column6: Le raisin que j'achète vient du marché.
column7: The grapes I buy come from the market.
column8: Masculine; in French it means a fresh grape, while dried ones are raisins secs.

column6: Cette épice vient d'Inde et sent très bon.
column7: This spice comes from India and smells very good.
column8: Feminine despite the initial vowel (l'épice); often used in the plural.

column6: Il met de la moutarde sur le jambon.
column7: He puts mustard on the ham.
column8: Feminine; the expression la moutarde monte au nez means to lose one's temper.

column6: Il ajoute du vinaigre dans la salade.
column7: He adds vinegar to the salad.
column8: Masculine; the final e is silent.

column6: La recette que ma mère utilise est simple.
column7: The recipe my mother uses is simple.
column8: Feminine; it can also mean the takings of a shop.

column6: Ce fromage a un goût très fort.
column7: This cheese has a very strong taste.
column8: Masculine; the circumflex does not change the sound and the final t is silent.

column6: Le plat que tu prépares sent bon.
column7: The dish you are preparing smells good.
column8: Masculine; it means a course or serving dish, while the individual plate is l'assiette.

column6: L'ingrédient qui manque est le sel.
column7: The ingredient that is missing is salt.
column8: Masculine; note the acute accent in the spelling.

column6: Nous allumons un feu dans la cheminée.
column7: We light a fire in the fireplace.
column8: Feminine; it also means the chimney stack.

column6: Les vieux livres sont dans le grenier.
column7: The old books are in the attic.
column8: Masculine; it can also mean a granary, but in a house it is the attic.

column6: Il tond la pelouse chaque samedi.
column7: He mows the lawn every Saturday.
column8: Feminine; it is a kept garden lawn, while a country meadow is a pré.

column6: Une clôture entoure le jardin.
column7: A fence surrounds the garden.
column8: Feminine; it has a circumflex and also means a closing.

column6: La clé ne tourne pas dans la serrure.
column7: The key does not turn in the lock.
column8: Feminine; a padlock is called a cadenas.

column6: Le robinet qui fuit est dans la cuisine.
column7: The tap that is leaking is in the kitchen.
column8: Masculine; the final t is silent.

column6: Il n'y a pas de prise près du lit.
column7: There is no socket near the bed.
column8: Feminine; the full form is prise de courant.

column6: Il faut changer cette ampoule.
column7: We need to change this bulb.
column8: Feminine; it also means a blister on the skin.

column6: Je n'ai plus de lessive.
column7: I have no more laundry detergent.
column8: Feminine; faire la lessive means to do the laundry.

column6: Il fait la vaisselle après le repas.
column7: He does the washing-up after the meal.
column8: Feminine and usually a collective singular: faire la vaisselle means to wash the dishes.

column6: Je range le balai dans le placard.
column7: I put the broom away in the cupboard.
column8: Masculine; the plural is balais.

column6: Passe l'éponge sur la table.
column7: Run the sponge over the table.
column8: Feminine; passer l'éponge also means to let a wrong go.

column6: Elle ferme le volet avant de dormir.
column7: She closes the shutter before sleeping.
column8: Masculine; usually found in the plural: les volets.

column6: Les verres sont dans le placard.
column7: The glasses are in the cupboard.
column8: Masculine; it is a built-in cupboard, while an armoire is a freestanding wardrobe.

column6: Le radiateur est froid ce matin.
column7: The radiator is cold this morning.
column8: Masculine; it also means a car radiator.

column6: Le chauffage ne marche pas.
column7: The heating does not work.
column8: Masculine; chauffage central is central heating.

column6: Le tuyau est cassé sous l'évier.
column7: The pipe is broken under the sink.
column8: Masculine; the plural is tuyaux, with an x.

column6: Il y a une fuite dans le toit.
column7: There is a leak in the roof.
column8: Feminine; it also means flight or escape, as in prendre la fuite.

column6: Le déménagement a lieu samedi prochain.
column7: The move takes place next Saturday.
column8: Masculine; the matching verb is déménager.

column6: On mange sur la terrasse quand il fait beau.
column7: We eat on the terrace when the weather is nice.
column8: Feminine; it also means the outdoor tables of a cafe.

column6: Ce matelas est trop dur.
column7: This mattress is too hard.
column8: Masculine; the final s is silent, and the plural is identical: des matelas.

column6: Il se brosse les dents au lavabo.
column7: He brushes his teeth at the washbasin.
column8: Masculine; in French it means the bathroom basin.

column6: Cette semaine, il y a une promotion.
column7: This week, there is a special offer.
column8: Feminine; it also means a career promotion.

column6: Je demande un remboursement au magasin.
column7: I am asking the shop for a refund.
column8: Masculine; the matching verb is rembourser.

column6: Gardez le reçu pour l'échange.
column7: Keep the receipt for the exchange.
column8: Masculine; it has the same form as the past participle of recevoir.

column6: L'emballage de ce produit est en carton.
column7: The packaging of this product is cardboard.
column8: Masculine; the matching verb is emballer.

column6: La vendeuse m'offre un échantillon de parfum.
column7: The saleswoman gives me a perfume sample.
column8: Masculine; it means a small example of a product.

column6: L'enseigne du magasin est très lumineuse.
column7: The shop sign is very bright.
column8: Feminine; it means a sign and also a retail chain.

column6: Le paquet que j'ai reçu est lourd.
column7: The packet I received is heavy.
column8: Masculine; it is a packet or pack, while a postal parcel is a colis.

column6: Quelle marque de café préférez-vous ?
column7: Which brand of coffee do you prefer?
column8: Feminine; it means a brand and also a mark or trace.

column6: Je préfère la qualité à la quantité.
column7: I prefer quality to quantity.
column8: Feminine; it also means a good trait of a person.

column6: Le produit que tu cherches est en rayon.
column7: The product you are looking for is on the shelf.
column8: Masculine; there is no final consonant sound.

column6: Mon dernier achat était un manteau.
column7: My last purchase was a coat.
column8: Masculine; the final t is silent. Faire des achats means to go shopping.

column6: La vente commence à neuf heures.
column7: The sale starts at nine o'clock.
column8: Feminine; en vente means for sale.

column6: La livraison arrive demain matin.
column7: The delivery arrives tomorrow morning.
column8: Feminine; the matching verb is livrer.

column6: Le tarif réduit est pour les étudiants.
column7: The reduced rate is for students.
column8: Masculine; it means an official price for a service.

column6: Notre budget est limité ce mois-ci.
column7: Our budget is limited this month.
column8: Masculine; the final t is silent.

column6: Cette dépense n'était pas prévue.
column7: This expense was not planned.
column8: Feminine; food shopping is called les courses instead.

column6: Il paie avec un chèque.
column7: He pays with a cheque.
column8: Masculine; British English spells it cheque, American English check.

column6: La boucherie ferme à midi.
column7: The butcher's shop closes at noon.
column8: Feminine; the shopkeeper is the boucher.

column6: Je cherche ce roman à la librairie.
column7: I am looking for this novel at the bookshop.
column8: False friend: librairie is a bookshop, while a library is a bibliothèque.

column6: Elle achète du lait et des pâtes à l'épicerie.
column7: She buys milk and pasta at the grocery shop.
column8: Feminine; it means a small food shop.

column6: Cette pâtisserie vend de bons gâteaux.
column7: This pastry shop sells good cakes.
column8: Feminine; it also means a single pastry: une pâtisserie.

column6: Le commerçant ferme sa boutique à dix-neuf heures.
column7: The shopkeeper closes his shop at seven p.m.
column8: Masculine; the feminine is commerçante.

column6: Nous avons changé notre itinéraire à cause de la neige.
column7: We changed our route because of the snow.
column8: Masculine noun despite the final -e. It refers to the planned path of a journey.

column6: Ils font une croisière en Méditerranée cet été.
column7: They are going on a cruise in the Mediterranean this summer.
column8: Feminine noun. It refers to a pleasure trip by ship with several stops.

column6: Nous avons dormi dans une petite auberge.
column7: We slept in a small inn.
column8: Feminine noun. In the phrase auberge de jeunesse it means a youth hostel.

column6: Quelle destination avez-vous choisie pour les vacances ?
column7: Which destination did you choose for the holidays?
column8: Feminine noun. It is also used in the phrase à destination de, meaning bound for.

column6: Le vol fait une escale à Francfort.
column7: The flight has a stopover in Frankfurt.
column8: Feminine noun. It refers to an intermediate stop of a flight or a ship.

column6: Le tourisme est important pour cette région.
column7: Tourism is important for this region.
column8: Masculine and uncountable noun: it is normally not used in the plural.

column6: Chaque voyageur doit présenter son billet.
column7: Every traveller must show their ticket.
column8: Masculine noun; the feminine is voyageuse. It refers to a person who travels, especially by train.

column6: Le trajet que nous avons choisi est court.
column7: The journey we chose is short.
column8: Masculine noun. It refers to the trip from one point to another, without the idea of a long voyage.

column6: Il faut payer le péage à la sortie.
column7: You have to pay the toll at the exit.
column8: Masculine noun. It means the toll and also the toll booth on a motorway.

column6: Il y a un embouteillage sur le périphérique.
column7: There is a traffic jam on the ring road.
column8: Masculine noun. It is often used in the plural: être dans les embouteillages.

column6: La navette va de l'aéroport au centre-ville.
column7: The shuttle goes from the airport to the city centre.
column8: Feminine noun. It is also used for the space shuttle.

column6: Le train arrive sur le quai numéro deux.
column7: The train is arriving on platform number two.
column8: Masculine noun. It also means a quay in a port or an embankment along a river in a city.

column6: Nous avons pris une location pour la semaine.
column7: We took a rental for the week.
column8: Feminine noun. False friend of English location: it means a rental or hire, not a place.

column6: Le licenciement a surpris tout le monde.
column7: The dismissal surprised everyone.
column8: Masculine noun. It refers to the end of a contract decided by the employer.

column6: Le candidat qui parle est très calme.
column7: The candidate who is speaking is very calm.
column8: Masculine noun; the feminine is candidate. It is used for an exam, a job interview or an election.

column6: J'ai envoyé ma candidature hier matin.
column7: I sent my application yesterday morning.
column8: Feminine noun. In the phrase poser sa candidature it means to apply.

column6: Cette entreprise prévoit une embauche importante en janvier.
column7: This company plans significant hiring in January.
column8: Feminine noun. It refers to the act of taking on an employee.

column6: Il a donné sa démission lundi.
column7: He handed in his resignation on Monday.
column8: Feminine noun, singular in French; in Italian the plural is usually used.

column6: Nous devons respecter cette échéance.
column7: We must meet this deadline.
column8: Feminine noun. It also means the due date of a payment.

column6: Chaque employé a une tâche précise.
column7: Each employee has a specific task.
column8: Feminine noun, with a circumflex on the a. Do not confuse it with tache (stain).

column6: Le syndicat qui défend les employés organise une grève.
column7: The union that defends the employees is organising a strike.
column8: Masculine noun. It means a trade union but also other kinds of association, such as the syndicat d'initiative.

column6: Elle prend un congé de trois semaines.
column7: She is taking three weeks of leave.
column8: Masculine noun. It is used for holidays, sickness and maternity: congé maladie, congé maternité.

column6: Il a une grande compétence en informatique.
column7: He has great skill in computing.
column8: Feminine noun. In a work context it is often used in the plural: les compétences.

column6: Ce logiciel est facile à installer.
column7: This software is easy to install.
column8: Masculine; it is the French word for «software».

column6: Cette société fabrique des meubles.
column7: This company makes furniture.
column8: Feminine noun. It means both a company and society in the general sense.

column6: Elle étudie la littérature française à l'université.
column7: She studies French literature at university.
column8: Written with a double t after the i: «littérature»; English «literature» has only one.

column6: Cet écrivain que je préfère vit à Lyon.
column7: The writer I prefer lives in Lyon.
column8: Masculine noun. It refers to someone who writes books.

column6: Cette sculpture est exposée dans le jardin du musée.
column7: This sculpture is displayed in the museum garden.
column8: Feminine noun; the person who makes it is a sculpteur.

column6: Ce village fait partie du patrimoine mondial.
column7: This village is part of the world heritage.
column8: Masculine noun. It also means the property inherited or owned by a person.

column6: Ce festival que nous aimons commence demain.
column7: This festival that we love starts tomorrow.
column8: Masculine noun. It refers to a music or film event, not a religious holiday.

column6: Cet orchestre joue ce soir à Paris.
column7: This orchestra is playing in Paris tonight.
column8: Masculine noun in French. It also means the stalls of a theatre.

column6: Cet acteur joue dans un film français.
column7: This actor is in a French film.
column8: Masculine noun; the feminine is actrice.

column6: Le réalisateur présente son nouveau film.
column7: The director is presenting his new film.
column8: Masculine noun; the feminine is réalisatrice. In the cinema it means the director.

column6: Les musiciens montent sur la scène.
column7: The musicians go up on the stage.
column8: Feminine noun. It also means a scene in a film or a play.

column6: Cette légende est très connue en Bretagne.
column7: This legend is very well known in Brittany.
column8: Feminine noun. It also means a caption under a photo or the key of a map.

column6: Ce monument date du dix-septième siècle.
column7: This monument dates from the seventeenth century.
column8: Masculine noun. A monument aux morts is a war memorial.

column6: Cette galerie expose des artistes locaux.
column7: This gallery shows local artists.
column8: Feminine noun. It also means a covered passage, for example a galerie marchande.

column6: C'est une coutume très ancienne dans la région.
column7: It is a very old custom in the region.
column8: Feminine noun. Do not confuse it with English costume: coutume means a custom or habit.

column6: Ce chanteur est très célèbre en France.
column7: This singer is very famous in France.
column8: Masculine noun; the feminine is chanteuse.

column6: Mon grand-père aime la pêche.
column7: My grandfather loves fishing.
column8: Feminine noun. The same word also means the fruit, the peach.

column6: Le jardinage est son passe-temps préféré.
column7: Gardening is her favourite pastime.
column8: Masculine and uncountable noun; it is based on the word jardin.

column6: Ce voyage était une vraie aventure.
column7: This trip was a real adventure.
column8: Feminine noun. It can also mean a short love affair.

column6: Le stade que tu vois est très ancien.
column7: The stadium you see is very old.
column8: Masculine noun. It also means a stage in a development, for example a stage of an illness.

column6: Chaque spectateur reçoit un petit programme.
column7: Every spectator gets a small programme.
column8: Masculine noun; the feminine is spectatrice.

column6: Notre entraînement commence à six heures.
column7: Our training starts at six o'clock.
column8: Masculine noun. It is used for sport but also for practising in general.

column6: La natation est un sport très complet.
column7: Swimming is a very complete sport.
column8: Feminine noun. It names the sport; the verb is nager.

column6: Il a gagné la course de vélo.
column7: He won the bike race.
column8: Feminine noun. In the plural, les courses also means grocery shopping.

column6: Elle a gagné à la loterie.
column7: She won the lottery.
column8: Feminine noun. It is also used figuratively: c'est une loterie means it is a matter of luck.

column6: Le cirque s'installe près du stade.
column7: The circus is setting up near the stadium.
column8: Masculine noun. In geography it also means a glacial cirque.

column6: Les enfants adorent ce manège.
column7: The children love this merry-go-round.
column8: Masculine noun. It also means a riding school.

column6: Le tournoi de tennis commence samedi.
column7: The tennis tournament starts on Saturday.
column8: Masculine noun, ending in -oi.

column6: Le chirurgien qui m'a opéré est très gentil.
column7: The surgeon who operated on me is very kind.
column8: Masculine noun. For a woman, une chirurgienne is the usual form.

column6: Le médecin demande une analyse de sang.
column7: The doctor orders a blood test.
column8: Feminine noun. In medical language it is often plural: faire des analyses.

column6: Il a la tension un peu élevée.
column7: His blood pressure is a bit high.
column8: Feminine noun. At the doctor's, it means blood pressure; it also means tension in general.

column6: Ce symptôme est très courant.
column7: This symptom is very common.
column8: Masculine noun, with a circumflex on the o.

column6: Le traitement dure deux semaines.
column7: The treatment lasts two weeks.
column8: Masculine noun. It also appears in traitement de texte, word processing.

column6: Il a une cicatrice sur le bras.
column7: He has a scar on his arm.
column8: Feminine noun, very similar to the Italian word.

column6: Elle a une fracture du poignet.
column7: She has a fractured wrist.
column8: Feminine noun, as in Italian.

column6: Une ambulance arrive en dix minutes.
column7: An ambulance is arriving in ten minutes.
column8: Feminine noun. The pronunciation starts with a nasal vowel.

column6: Elle prend une pilule chaque matin.
column7: She takes a pill every morning.
column8: Feminine noun. La pilule often means the contraceptive pill.

column6: Ce médecin prescrit rarement un antibiotique.
column7: This doctor rarely prescribes an antibiotic.
column8: Masculine noun; it is also used as an adjective.

column6: J'ai une migraine depuis ce matin.
column7: I have had a migraine since this morning.
column8: Feminine noun. It means a severe headache.

column6: Nous espérons une guérison rapide.
column7: We hope for a quick recovery.
column8: Feminine noun, formed from the verb guérir.

column6: Le diagnostic arrive demain matin.
column7: The diagnosis will come tomorrow morning.
column8: Masculine noun. The French word is diagnostic, not diagnosis.

column6: Ce livre peut valoir cent euros.
column7: This book can be worth a hundred euros.
column8: Irregular verb: il vaut in the present, past participle valu. The phrase il vaut mieux means "it is better".

column6: Un seul jour ne va pas suffire.
column7: One day alone will not be enough.
column8: Irregular verb: nous suffisons, past participle suffi. It is often used impersonally: il suffit de + infinitive.

column6: Il ne faut pas craindre le médecin.
column7: You must not be afraid of the doctor.
column8: Irregular verb: je crains, nous craignons, past participle craint. It takes a noun or que + subjunctive.

column6: Nous voulons atteindre le sommet avant midi.
column7: We want to reach the summit before noon.
column8: Irregular verb like peindre: j'atteins, nous atteignons, past participle atteint. It takes a direct object, with no preposition.

column6: Il veut poursuivre ses études à Lyon.
column7: He wants to continue his studies in Lyon.
column8: Conjugated like suivre; past participle poursuivi. It can mean "to chase" or "to continue".

column6: Je vais convaincre mon patron de venir.
column7: I am going to convince my boss to come.
column8: Irregular verb like vaincre: il convainc (no final t), nous convainquons, past participle convaincu. The pattern is convaincre qqn de + infinitive.

column6: Il faut prévoir un parapluie demain.
column7: You need to plan for an umbrella tomorrow.
column8: Conjugated like voir, but the future is je prévoirai; past participle prévu. It means "to foresee" and "to schedule".

column6: Cette région peut produire du bon vin.
column7: This region can produce good wine.
column8: Conjugated like conduire: nous produisons, past participle produit.

column6: Vous devez remettre ce dossier lundi.
column7: You must hand over this file on Monday.
column8: Conjugated like mettre; past participle remis. It also means "to put back" and "to postpone" (remettre à plus tard).

column6: Ce menu peut satisfaire tout le monde.
column7: This menu can satisfy everyone.
column8: Conjugated like faire: nous satisfaisons, past participle satisfait. Satisfaire qqn is direct; satisfaire à qqch means "to meet a requirement".

column6: Je vais rejoindre mes amis à la gare.
column7: I am going to join my friends at the station.
column8: Conjugated like joindre: nous rejoignons, past participle rejoint. It is used for joining people or reaching places.

column6: Nous devons soutenir ce projet local.
column7: We must support this local project.
column8: Conjugated like tenir: il soutient, nous soutenons, past participle soutenu; auxiliary avoir.

column6: Tu peux sentir cette odeur ?
column7: Can you smell this odor?
column8: Irregular verb: je sens, nous sentons, past participle senti. It means to feel a sensation or smell something, and also "to smell of": ça sent bon.

column6: On va servir le dîner à huit heures.
column7: We are going to serve dinner at eight o'clock.
column8: Irregular verb: je sers, nous servons, past participle servi. Se servir de means "to use".

column6: Il faut cuire ce poulet une heure.
column7: You have to cook this chicken for an hour.
column8: Irregular verb: je cuis, nous cuisons, past participle cuit. Faire cuire is also common.

column6: Nous allons résoudre ce problème ensemble.
column7: We are going to solve this problem together.
column8: Irregular verb: je résous, nous résolvons, past participle résolu. It takes a direct object: résoudre un problème.

column6: Tu dois prévenir ton médecin demain.
column7: You must notify your doctor tomorrow.
column8: Conjugated like venir but with the auxiliary avoir; past participle prévenu. The pattern is prévenir qqn de qqch.

column6: On va interdire les voitures ici.
column7: They are going to ban cars here.
column8: Conjugated like dire, but the vous form is vous interdisez; past participle interdit.

column6: Cette nouvelle va surprendre ma famille.
column7: This news is going to surprise my family.
column8: Conjugated like prendre: nous surprenons, past participle surpris. It can also mean "to catch someone in the act".

column6: Il faut admettre son erreur.
column7: You have to admit your mistake.
column8: Conjugated like mettre; past participle admis. It also means "to admit" someone to a school or a place.

column6: On peut apercevoir la mer d'ici.
column7: You can catch a glimpse of the sea from here.
column8: Conjugated like recevoir: j'aperçois, nous apercevons, past participle aperçu. It means to see something briefly or from a distance.

column6: Merci de joindre une photo récente.
column7: Please attach a recent photo.
column8: Conjugated like peindre: nous joignons, past participle joint. It is used for attaching a document or joining two things.

column6: Tu peux plaindre ton frère, il travaille tous les week-ends.
column7: You can feel sorry for your brother, he works every weekend.
column8: Conjugated like craindre: nous plaignons, past participle plaint. Se plaindre means "to complain".

column6: Hier, elle a adoré ce petit hôtel.
column7: Yesterday she loved this little hotel.
column8: Regular -er verb; it takes a direct object: adorer un film.

column6: Samedi, vous avez apporté un beau gâteau.
column7: On Saturday you brought a lovely cake.
column8: Regular -er verb; it is used for bringing an object (for a person amener is preferred).

column6: Hier, il a augmenté ses prix.
column7: Yesterday he raised his prices.
column8: Regular -er verb; it can be transitive (augmenter les prix) or intransitive (les prix augmentent).

column6: Hier, ils ont caché un cadeau ici.
column7: Yesterday they hid a present here.
column8: Regular -er verb; se cacher means "to hide oneself".

column6: Hier, il a créé une nouvelle marque.
column7: Yesterday he created a new brand.
column8: Regular -er verb; the past participle créé has two é (feminine créée).

column6: Samedi, nous avons échangé nos numéros.
column7: On Saturday we swapped phone numbers.
column8: Regular -er verb; before a and o the g becomes ge: nous échangeons.

column6: Hier, ils ont fabriqué ce meuble.
column7: Yesterday they made this piece of furniture.
column8: Regular -er verb; it means "to make" and is also used for "to invent" (fabriquer une excuse).

column6: Ce mois-ci, tu as gaspillé trop d'eau.
column7: This month you wasted too much water.
column8: Regular -er verb; the double l is pronounced like a y sound (ɡaspije).

column6: Ce matin, nous avons noté ton adresse.
column7: This morning we noted down your address.
column8: Regular -er verb; it means "to jot down" but also "to grade".

column6: Hier, il a observé des oiseaux longtemps.
column7: Yesterday he watched some birds for a long time.
column8: Regular -er verb; it takes a direct object: observer des oiseaux.

column6: Hier, tu as réagi trop vite.
column7: Yesterday you reacted too quickly.
column8: Regular verb like finir: nous réagissons, past participle réagi. It takes à: réagir à qqch.

column6: Hier, elle a saisi sa chance.
column7: Yesterday she seized her chance.
column8: Regular verb like finir: nous saisissons, past participle saisi. It means "to grab" and also "to seize" an opportunity.

column6: Samedi, vous avez réuni toute la famille.
column7: On Saturday you gathered the whole family.
column8: Regular verb like finir: nous réunissons, past participle réuni. Se réunir means "to meet up".

column6: Hier, ils ont fourni tous les ingrédients.
column7: Yesterday they supplied all the ingredients.
column8: Regular verb like finir: nous fournissons, past participle fourni. The pattern is fournir qqch à qqn.

column6: Je la chauffe cinq minutes.
column7: I heat it for five minutes.
column8: Regular -er verb, transitive or intransitive; se chauffer means "to warm oneself up".

column6: Ils le critiquent sans cesse.
column7: They criticize him all the time.
column8: Regular -er verb; it takes a direct object: critiquer qqn ou qqch.

column6: Il les évite pour sa santé.
column7: He avoids them for his health.
column8: Regular -er verb; it takes a direct object or de + infinitive: éviter de fumer.

column6: Nous les mélangeons avec du sucre.
column7: We mix them with sugar.
column8: Regular -er verb; before a and o the g becomes ge: nous mélangeons.

column6: Il la répand sur mon tapis.
column7: He spreads it on my rug.
column8: Regular -re verb like vendre: je répands, past participle répandu. Se répandre also means "to spread" in the sense of "to become widespread".

column6: Nous la poussons doucement.
column7: We push it gently.
column8: Regular -er verb; it can mean "to push" or "to grow" (of plants).

column6: Je les rassure toujours.
column7: I always reassure them.
column8: Regular -er verb; se rassurer means "to reassure oneself".

column6: Nous la réglons demain.
column7: We settle it tomorrow.
column8: Regular verb with an accent change: je règle, nous réglons. It also means "to pay" a bill.

column6: Nous les remplacerons demain.
column7: We will replace them tomorrow.
column8: Regular -er verb; before a and o the c becomes ç: nous remplaçons.

column6: Elle les respecte beaucoup.
column7: She respects them a lot.
column8: Regular -er verb; it takes a direct object: respecter les règles.

column6: Il le retire de son sac.
column7: He takes it out of his bag.
column8: Regular -er verb; it means "to take out" and also "to withdraw" (money).

column6: Ils la sauvent à temps.
column7: They save her in time.
column8: Regular -er verb; se sauver means "to run away".

column6: Vous le signez ici.
column7: You sign it here.
column8: Regular -er verb; the group gn is pronounced ɲ, as in Italian.

column6: Je la soigne chez moi.
column7: I treat her at my place.
column8: Regular -er verb; it means "to treat" and also "to take care of".

column6: Nous bavardions souvent au café.
column7: We often chatted at the cafe.
column8: Regular -er verb, intransitive; the pattern is bavarder avec qqn.

column6: Le film durait trois heures.
column7: The film lasted three hours.
column8: Regular -er verb, intransitive; it expresses the duration of an event.

column6: Cette vieille machine fonctionnait bien.
column7: This old machine worked well.
column8: Regular -er verb, intransitive; it is used for machines and systems.

column6: Mon père fumait beaucoup autrefois.
column7: My father used to smoke a lot.
column8: Regular -er verb; it is used with or without an object: fumer une cigarette.

column6: Nous roulions lentement vers Lyon.
column7: We were driving slowly towards Lyon.
column8: Regular -er verb, intransitive for vehicles and their drivers; auxiliary avoir.

column6: Elle imaginera un nouveau décor.
column7: She will imagine a new set design.
column8: Regular -er verb; s'imaginer means "to picture to oneself".

column6: Nous informerons nos clients lundi.
column7: We will inform our customers on Monday.
column8: Regular -er verb; the pattern is informer qqn de qqch.

column6: Tu regretteras cet achat.
column7: You will regret this purchase.
column8: Regular -er verb; it takes de + infinitive or que + subjunctive.

column6: Tu respireras mieux à la montagne.
column7: You will breathe better in the mountains.
column8: Regular -er verb; it can be transitive or intransitive.

column6: Nous établirons un nouveau plan.
column7: We will draw up a new plan.
column8: Regular verb like finir: nous établissons, past participle établi. S'établir means "to settle".

column6: Je poserais une question au guide.
column7: I would ask the guide a question.
column8: Regular -er verb; poser une question means "to ask a question" (faire is not used).

column6: On pourrait agir autrement ici.
column7: We could act differently here.
column8: Regular verb like finir: nous agissons, past participle agi. Il s'agit de means "it is about".

column6: Elle rougirait de honte.
column7: She would blush with shame.
column8: Regular verb like finir: nous rougissons; it is intransitive (rougir de honte).

column6: Je ne prétendrais pas tout savoir.
column7: I would not claim to know everything.
column8: Regular -re verb. False friend: prétendre means "to claim", while Italian "pretendere" is exiger.

column6: Baissez la voix, s'il vous plaît !
column7: Lower your voice, please!
column8: Regular -er verb; it is also used in baisser les yeux (to look down).

column6: Ne pleurez pas, tout ira bien !
column7: Do not cry, everything will be fine!
column8: Regular -er verb, intransitive; pleurer de joie means "to cry for joy".

column6: Avertissez le guide en cas de problème !
column7: Warn the guide if there is a problem!
column8: Regular verb like finir: nous avertissons, past participle averti. The pattern is avertir qqn de qqch.

column6: Tendez votre billet au contrôleur !
column7: Hand your ticket to the inspector!
column8: Regular -re verb like vendre: je tends, past participle tendu. Tendre la main means "to hold out one's hand".

column6: Ce film me touche beaucoup.
column7: This film touches me a lot.
column8: Regular -er verb; toucher qqn can also mean "to move" someone; toucher un salaire means "to receive a salary".

column6: Cette erreur nous coûte cher.
column7: This mistake costs us a lot.
column8: Regular -er verb; it is mostly used in the third person: ça coûte, ça coûtait.

column6: Ça ne me gêne pas du tout.
column7: That does not bother me at all.
column8: Regular -er verb; it means "to bother" or "to make uncomfortable". The circumflex stays in every form.

column6: Je leur montre ma chambre.
column7: I show them my room.
column8: Regular -er verb; it takes a direct and an indirect object: montrer qqch à qqn.

column6: Nous en profitons beaucoup.
column7: We make the most of it.
column8: Regular -er verb; it takes de: profiter de qqch, hence the pronoun en.

column6: Nous y logeons depuis juin.
column7: We have been staying there since June.
column8: Regular -er verb; before a and o the g becomes ge: nous logeons.

column6: Ils en livrent chaque matin.
column7: They deliver some every morning.
column8: Regular -er verb. Watch out: livrer means "to deliver", while "book" is livre.

column6: Nous nous disputons pour rien.
column7: We quarrel over nothing.
column8: Regular -er verb; in its pronominal form se disputer means "to quarrel".

column6: Elle se fâche très vite.
column7: She gets angry very quickly.
column8: Regular -er verb; se fâcher means "to get angry" and se fâcher avec qqn means "to fall out with someone".

column6: Ils se baignent dans le lac.
column7: They go for a swim in the lake.
column8: Regular -er verb; se baigner means "to go for a swim"; baigner qqn means "to bathe someone".

column6: Je me trompe de direction.
column7: I am going the wrong way.
column8: Regular -er verb; se tromper de + noun means "to get the wrong one" (se tromper de route); tromper qqn means "to deceive".

column6: Ils se marient en juin.
column7: They are getting married in June.
column8: Regular -er verb; se marier avec qqn means "to marry someone"; in compound tenses it uses être: ils se sont mariés.

column6: Nous nous entraînons chaque matin.
column7: We train every morning.
column8: Regular -er verb; s'entraîner means "to train oneself"; the circumflex stays in every form.

column6: Je me renseigne sur les horaires.
column7: I am finding out about the timetables.
column8: Regular -er verb; se renseigner sur means "to find out about"; renseigner qqn means "to give someone information".

column6: Tu te détends au parc ?
column7: Do you relax at the park?
column8: Regular -re verb like vendre: je détends, past participle détendu; se détendre means "to relax".

column6: Tu risques de rater ton train.
column7: You are at risk of missing your train.
column8: Regular -er verb; risquer de + infinitive means "to risk doing" and points to a possibly bad outcome.

column6: Je suppose que vous avez faim.
column7: I suppose you are hungry.
column8: Regular -er verb; je suppose que is followed by the indicative.

column6: Ce sac est très pratique pour voyager.
column7: This bag is very practical for travelling.
column8: Same form for masculine and feminine; the plural is pratiques.

column6: Cette formation est nécessaire pour le poste.
column7: This training is necessary for the position.
column8: Same form in the masculine and feminine; often used in il est nécessaire de + infinitive.

column6: Mon fauteuil habituel est près de la fenêtre.
column7: My usual armchair is near the window.
column8: The feminine is habituelle, with a doubled l.

column6: Voici une application utile que j'ai achetée hier.
column7: Here is a useful app that I bought yesterday.
column8: Same form in the masculine and feminine; the opposite is inutile.

column6: La recette est simple et rapide.
column7: The recipe is simple and quick.
column8: Same form in the masculine and feminine. Before a noun (un simple geste) it means "mere".

column6: Chaque pays a une cuisine différente.
column7: Every country has a different cuisine.
column8: The feminine is différente; it takes de: différent de.

column6: L'entrée du musée est gratuite le dimanche.
column7: Museum admission is free on Sundays.
column8: The feminine is gratuite. It means free of charge, not free in the sense of libre.

column6: Voici le pain frais que j'ai acheté.
column7: Here is the fresh bread that I bought.
column8: The feminine is fraîche. It also describes a cool temperature.

column6: L'hôtel est complet ce week-end.
column7: The hotel is full this weekend.
column8: The feminine is complète. On a hotel or car park sign it means fully booked.

column6: Le directeur est disponible demain matin.
column7: The director is available tomorrow morning.
column8: Same form in the masculine and feminine.

column6: Elle parle trois langues étrangères.
column7: She speaks three foreign languages.
column8: The feminine is étrangère; it is also a noun (un étranger: a foreigner).

column6: C'est un quartier touristique qui me plaît.
column7: It is a tourist district that I like.
column8: Same form in the masculine and feminine; used for places and activities linked to tourism.

column6: Le jardin public ferme à vingt heures.
column7: The public garden closes at eight p.m.
column8: The feminine is publique (note the -que ending); it is also a noun (le public: the audience).

column6: Ce musée d'art moderne est magnifique.
column7: This modern art museum is magnificent.
column8: Same form in the masculine and feminine.

column6: C'est une danse typique que j'aime.
column7: It is a typical dance that I like.
column8: Same form in the masculine and feminine; often used with de: typique de la région.

column6: Nous visitons un centre culturel demain.
column7: We are visiting a cultural centre tomorrow.
column8: The feminine is culturelle, with a doubled l.

column6: Mon frère est très sportif.
column7: My brother is very sporty.
column8: The feminine is sportive (f becomes v).

column6: Les enfants sont curieux de tout.
column7: Children are curious about everything.
column8: The feminine is curieuse. It can also mean odd: une histoire curieuse.

column6: Ce film est long et ennuyeux.
column7: This film is long and boring.
column8: The feminine is ennuyeuse; it describes what bores, not the person who is bored.

column6: Ce jeu amusant que tu m'as offert est génial.
column7: This fun game that you gave me is great.
column8: The feminine is amusante; it describes what amuses.

column6: Il est fier de son équipe.
column7: He is proud of his team.
column8: The feminine is fière, with a grave accent; it takes de.

column6: Il est malheureux sans son chien.
column7: He is unhappy without his dog.
column8: The feminine is malheureuse; it is the opposite of heureux.

column6: Je suis enrhumé depuis lundi.
column7: I have had a cold since Monday.
column8: The feminine is enrhumée; it is used with être: je suis enrhumé.

column6: Ce repas est sain et léger.
column7: This meal is healthy and light.
column8: The feminine is saine; used for food, habits and environments.

column6: Le joueur est blessé au genou.
column7: The player is injured in the knee.
column8: The feminine is blessée; it is also a noun (un blessé: an injured person).

column6: Ce voyage est long et fatigant.
column7: This trip is long and tiring.
column8: The feminine is fatigante; it describes what tires, while fatigué describes the person.

column6: J'ai une expérience professionnelle de trois ans.
column7: I have three years of professional experience.
column8: The feminine is professionnelle, with doubled n and l.

column6: Donnez-moi une réponse précise, s'il vous plaît.
column7: Give me a precise answer, please.
column8: The feminine is précise. It is also used for exact times: à midi précis.

column6: La date indiquée n'est pas exacte.
column7: The date given is not correct.
column8: The feminine is exacte; used for figures, information and measurements.

column6: Il fait un effort régulier chaque jour.
column7: He makes a regular effort every day.
column8: The feminine is régulière.

column6: Cette offre spéciale finit demain.
column7: This special offer ends tomorrow.
column8: The feminine is spéciale; the masculine plural is spéciaux, like adjectives in -al.

column6: Ce nouveau supermarché est énorme.
column7: This new supermarket is huge.
column8: Same form in the masculine and feminine; the plural is énormes.

column6: Ce canapé est très confortable.
column7: This sofa is very comfortable.
column8: Same form in the masculine and feminine. For a person who feels at ease, use être à l'aise.

column6: La salle de bain est humide.
column7: The bathroom is damp.
column8: Same form in the masculine and feminine; the initial h is silent.

column6: Notre nouveau salon est très spacieux.
column7: Our new living room is very spacious.
column8: The feminine is spacieuse.

column6: Ce petit studio est très lumineux.
column7: This small studio is very bright.
column8: The feminine is lumineuse.

column6: Attention, ce verre est très fragile.
column7: Careful, this glass is very fragile.
column8: Same form in the masculine and feminine.

column6: Il y a un train direct pour Lyon.
column7: There is a direct train to Lyon.
column8: The feminine is directe; un train direct is a train with no change.

column6: Je suis récemment arrivé dans cette entreprise.
column7: I recently arrived at this company.
column8: Adverbs in -emment are pronounced -amɑ̃. It often sits between the auxiliary and the participle.

column6: Il y a beaucoup de musées, notamment le Louvre.
column7: There are many museums, notably the Louvre.
column8: It introduces one example among others and usually follows a comma.

column6: Fais attention, autrement tu vas tomber.
column7: Be careful, otherwise you are going to fall.
column8: It means both otherwise and in a different way; here it introduces a consequence.

column6: Désormais, je ne mange pas de viande.
column7: From now on, I do not eat meat.
column8: It often opens a sentence, followed by a comma.

column6: Je voudrais davantage de café, s'il vous plaît.
column7: I would like more coffee, please.
column8: Used alone or with de: davantage de café. It is not used before an adjective (use plus grand).

column6: Il fera probablement beau demain.
column7: It will probably be nice tomorrow.
column8: Formed from probable plus -ment; usually placed after the verb or auxiliary.

column6: Si vous avez de la fièvre, appelez immédiatement un médecin.
column7: If you have a fever, call a doctor immediately.
column8: A more formal synonym of tout de suite.

column6: Autrefois, nous sortions rarement le soir.
column7: In the past, we rarely went out in the evening.
column8: It is the opposite of souvent; usually placed after the verb.

column6: Généralement, j'ai faim à midi.
column7: Usually, I am hungry at noon.
column8: A synonym of en général; often at the start of a sentence, followed by a comma.

column6: Tu as absolument raison !
column7: You are absolutely right!
column8: It can also be an answer on its own: Absolument! means "absolutely, yes".

column6: Nous avons également un jardin.
column7: We also have a garden.
column8: More formal than aussi.

column6: Soudain, j'ai mal à la tête.
column7: Suddenly, I have a headache.
column8: As an adverb it is invariable; it is also an adjective (un départ soudain).

column6: Durant l'été, il y a beaucoup de touristes.
column7: During the summer, there are many tourists.
column8: More formal and written than pendant: durant le film.

column6: Le musée est ouvert tous les jours sauf lundi.
column7: The museum is open every day except Monday.
column8: Usually followed by a noun without an article: sauf lundi. Followed by si it means unless: sauf si.

column6: Toute la famille est autour de la table.
column7: The whole family is around the table.
column8: Almost always used with de: autour de la table.

column6: Dès demain, je vais courir tous les matins.
column7: From tomorrow, I am going to run every morning.
column8: It marks a starting point in time: dès lundi. Not to be confused with des (article).

column6: Le prix est élevé, cependant la qualité est excellente.
column7: The price is high, however the quality is excellent.
column8: More formal than mais; usually preceded by a comma or a full stop.

column6: Le travail est difficile, toutefois il est intéressant.
column7: The work is difficult, nevertheless it is interesting.
column8: A formal synonym of cependant, more common in writing.

column6: Il n'y a ni pain ni lait.
column7: There is neither bread nor milk.
column8: Repeated before each element and used with ne before the verb.

column6: Soit nous irons à la mer, soit nous resterons ici.
column7: Either we will go to the sea, or we will stay here.
column8: Repeated: soit… soit…. It has the same form as the subjunctive of être (qu'il soit).

column6: Personne n'est à la maison.
column7: Nobody is at home.
column8: With ne before the verb it means nobody. As a noun (une personne) it means person and is always feminine.

column6: Aucun de ces livres n'est cher.
column7: None of these books is expensive.
column8: The feminine is aucune; used with ne and usually in the singular.

column6: Certains ont mal au dos après le voyage.
column7: Some people have a backache after the trip.
column8: The feminine is certaines; it is also an adjective before a noun (certaines personnes).

column6: C'est le roman dont je te parle.
column7: It is the novel I am telling you about.
column8: It replaces de + noun: parler de ce livre becomes le livre dont je parle. It never elides.

column6: Celui qui parle est mon voisin.
column7: The one who is speaking is my neighbour.
column8: The feminine is celle, the plurals are ceux and celles; used with qui, que or de.

column6: Cela ne coûte pas cher.
column7: That does not cost much.
column8: More formal than ça; it refers to something already mentioned.

column6: Regardez ceci, c'est un cadeau pour vous.
column7: Look at this, it is a gift for you.
column8: It points to something close or about to be said; often contrasted with cela.

column6: De quoi as-tu besoin ?
column7: What do you need?
column8: Used after a preposition (de quoi, à quoi) and as an informal question at the end of a sentence.

column6: Il est retombé malade hier.
column7: He fell ill again yesterday.
column8: In the passé composé it takes être, like the verb it is built on.

column6: Nous sommes redescendus au salon.
column7: We came back down to the living room.
column8: It is a regular -re verb; used without an object it takes être in the passé composé.

column6: Le soleil va disparaître derrière la colline.
column7: The sun is going to disappear behind the hill.
column8: It is irregular, with î before t (il disparaît); the past participle is disparu.

column6: Mon nom est parmi les gagnants.
column7: My name is among the winners.
column8: It is used only before a plural or a group.

column6: Je suis triste lorsque mon fils part.
column7: I am sad when my son leaves.
column8: It elides before il, elle, on, un, une: lorsqu'il. It is more formal than quand.

column6: Puisque tu es fatigué, tu restes ici.
column7: Since you are tired, you are staying here.
column8: It introduces a reason the listener already knows. It elides before il, elle, on: puisqu'il.

column6: Lequel est ton vélo ?
column7: Which one is your bike?
column8: It agrees: laquelle, lesquels, lesquelles. It is used to choose among known items.

column6: Il m'a donné un bon conseil.
column7: He gave me good advice.
column8: In the singular it is also a council or board (le conseil municipal).

column6: À mon avis, ce film est trop long.
column7: In my opinion, this film is too long.
column8: The plural is the same as the singular: «les avis»; the final s is silent.

column6: J'ai l'habitude de me lever tôt.
column7: I am used to getting up early.
column8: It is often used in «avoir l'habitude de» + infinitive.

column6: J'ai un très bon souvenir de ce voyage.
column7: I have a very good memory of this trip.
column8: It means both a memory and a tourist souvenir.

column6: Il faut protéger l'environnement.
column7: We must protect the environment.
column8: It is written with a double n: «environnement».

column6: J'ai reçu un colis ce matin.
column7: I received a parcel this morning.
column8: It is invariable: «un colis», «des colis»; the final s is silent.

column6: Il y a trop de bruit dans la rue.
column7: There is too much noise in the street.
column8: It also means a rumour («un bruit court»); here it is noise.

column6: Le mariage a lieu en juin.
column7: The wedding takes place in June.
column8: It means both the ceremony and the state of marriage.

column6: Le propriétaire vend la maison.
column7: The owner is selling the house.
column8: It is masculine or feminine according to the person: «le/la propriétaire».

column6: Elle a beaucoup d'expérience dans ce métier.
column7: She has a lot of experience in this job.
column8: It also means an experiment: «une expérience scientifique».

column6: Nous hésitons encore entre deux hôtels.
column7: We are still hesitating between two hotels.
column8: It takes «à» + infinitive: «hésiter à partir».

column6: Tu me manques beaucoup.
column7: I miss you a lot.
column8: «Tu me manques» = I miss you: the person who is missed is the subject.

column6: Nous avons emménagé en septembre.
column7: We moved in in September.
column8: It is the opposite of «déménager» (moving out of a home).

column6: Je m'occupe de mes enfants le soir.
column7: I look after my children in the evening.
column8: It takes «de»: «s'occuper de» + noun or infinitive.

column6: Nous nous habituons vite à cette ville.
column7: We get used to this city quickly.
column8: It takes «à»: «s'habituer à» + noun or infinitive.

column6: Je prendrais volontiers un autre café.
column7: I would gladly have another coffee.
column8: Also used alone as a polite answer to an offer.

column6: Le gouvernement a annoncé de nouvelles mesures hier.
column7: The government announced new measures yesterday.
column8: Related to the verb gouverner; it refers to the executive.

column6: Le journaliste qui écrit cet article connaît le sujet.
column7: The journalist who writes this article knows the subject.
column8: Same form for both genders (le/la journaliste).

column6: Le jardinage est devenu sa passion depuis la retraite.
column7: Gardening has become his passion since retirement.
column8: Also used for a hobby pursued with great commitment.

column6: Cet impôt est prélevé directement sur le salaire.
column7: This tax is deducted straight from the salary.
column8: It carries a circumflex and is the general state levy, whereas "taxe" is usually tied to a service or product.

column6: Après le déjeuner, nous avons fait une longue balade.
column7: After lunch, we went for a long stroll.
column8: It is more informal than the standard word for a walk and is used with faire: faire une balade.

column6: Les élèves déjeunent à la cantine de l'école.
column7: The pupils have lunch at the school canteen.
column8: It means a school or company canteen. It does not mean a wine cellar.

column6: Nous avons atteint le sommet avant midi.
column7: We reached the summit before noon.
column8: It means the top of a mountain. In politics it is also a summit between heads of state.

column6: Le plombier viendra demain matin réparer le robinet.
column7: The plumber will come tomorrow morning to repair the tap.
column8: It means plumber; it comes from «plomb» (lead), like English «plumber».

column6: Si tu veux bronzer, mets d'abord de la crème solaire.
column7: If you want to tan, put on sunscreen first.
column8: Both «bronzer» (intransitive) and «se bronzer» are used: «je bronze vite», «je me bronze au soleil».

column6: L'avion décolle dans vingt minutes.
column7: The plane takes off in twenty minutes.
column8: It is said of planes and rockets. It also means to peel off, for example a label.

column6: Ils naviguent depuis l'aube sur une mer calme.
column7: They have been sailing since dawn on a calm sea.
column8: It applies to boats and ships, and also to the web: naviguer sur Internet.

column6: Je n'aime pas le café tiède.
column7: I do not like lukewarm coffee.
column8: It has the same form in the feminine. It means neither hot nor cold, often unpleasantly so.

column6: Le carnaval de Nice attire des milliers de visiteurs.
column7: The Nice carnival attracts thousands of visitors.
column8: The plural is «carnavals»; it denotes the festival that precedes Lent.
